mcqs.question: Which of the following descriptions correctly visualises three lines that intersect each other pairwise but do not all meet at a single point?

options.A: All three lines cross at the same point, forming a star‑shaped figure.
options.B: Two of the lines are parallel and the third line cuts across both of them.
options.C: Each line meets the other two at different points, producing three distinct intersection points that form a triangle.
options.D: All three lines are parallel and never meet.

mcqs.answer: Each line meets the other two at different points, producing three distinct intersection points that form a triangle.
mcqs.explanation: When three lines intersect pairwise at three different points, they create a triangular arrangement. Option C describes this correctly. Option A shows concurrency (a common misconception), B gives only two intersections, and D gives no intersections.

mcqs.question: Line l1 meets line l2 at point A, line l2 meets line l3 at point B, and line l1 meets line l3 at point C. How many distinct intersection points are there among the three lines?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of lines meets at a unique point: l1‑l2 at A, l2‑l3 at B, and l1‑l3 at C. Hence there are three distinct intersection points. The other options underestimate the count.

mcqs.question: In a configuration where three lines intersect pairwise at three different points, which statement correctly compares the angles at each intersection?

options.A: All six angles at a single intersection are equal.
options.B: Opposite (vertical) angles are equal, and each pair of adjacent angles adds up to 180°.
options.C: No two angles are equal at any intersection.
options.D: All angles formed are right angles.

mcqs.answer: Opposite (vertical) angles are equal, and each pair of adjacent angles adds up to 180°.
mcqs.explanation: When two lines cross, they create two pairs of vertical angles that are equal, while each pair of adjacent angles are supplementary (sum to 180°). This property holds at each of the three intersection points. Options A, C, and D are incorrect descriptions.

mcqs.question: A competitive exam asks: Which arrangement of three straight lines will give exactly three distinct points of intersection and form a triangle?

options.A: All three lines pass through a single common point.
options.B: Two of the lines are parallel while the third cuts across them.
options.C: Each line intersects the other two at different points, producing three intersection points.
options.D: One line coincides with another line, and the third line is separate.

mcqs.answer: Each line intersects the other two at different points, producing three intersection points.
mcqs.explanation: Only when each pair of lines meets at a separate point do we obtain three distinct intersections that outline a triangle. Option A gives one intersection, B gives two, and D reduces the number of distinct lines, so they do not satisfy the condition.

mcqs.question: Which description best matches a picture where three lines intersect each other at three different points?

options.A: All three lines meet at a single point, forming a star shape.
options.B: Two lines intersect while the third line runs parallel to both.
options.C: Each line meets the other two at separate points, creating three distinct intersections.
options.D: All three lines are parallel and never intersect.

mcqs.answer: Each line meets the other two at separate points, creating three distinct intersections.
mcqs.explanation: The correct visualisation is when every pair of lines crosses at its own point, giving three intersection points. Options A, B, and D describe different configurations that do not meet the requirement.

mcqs.question: When three straight lines intersect each other at different points, how many intersection points are formed?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of lines meets once, giving three pairs and therefore three distinct intersection points. The other numbers are too low or imply no intersections.

mcqs.question: In the context of three intersecting lines, which statement correctly defines vertical angles?

options.A: Vertical angles are the angles that share a common side.
options.B: Vertical angles are the opposite angles formed when two lines cross; they are equal in measure.
options.C: Vertical angles are always right angles.
options.D: Vertical angles are adjacent angles that add up to 90°.

mcqs.answer: Vertical angles are the opposite angles formed when two lines cross; they are equal in measure.
mcqs.explanation: Vertical angles are the non‑adjacent angles opposite each other at an intersection of two lines, and they are always equal. Options A, C, and D describe other relationships that are not the definition of vertical angles.

mcqs.question: A student draws three lines so that each line cuts the other two, creating a small triangle in the middle. How many points of intersection does this arrangement have?
mcqs.explanation: Each of the three lines meets the other two at a unique point, giving three intersection points. The triangle formed is bounded by those three points. The other options underestimate or overestimate the count.
